questions.question: What is a Gemfile and how do you read one?
questions.title: The Gemfile
questions.direct_answer: A Gemfile is the file listing the Ruby gems your app depends on. It starts with source 'https://rubygems.org' (where to fetch gems), then gem lines: gem 'rails', '~> 7.0' (name + version constraint). Version constraints: '~> 7.0' means >= 7.0, < 8.0 (pessimistic; allows patch/minor), '7.0.1' pins exact, '>= 7' any 7+. You group gems with :group (gem 'rspec', group: :test) so they're not loaded in prod, and pin sources for git gems (gem 'x', github: 'org/x'). After editing, run bundle install to resolve and write Gemfile.lock.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can read a Gemfile (source, gem + version constraint, groups), and know the version constraint syntax (~> vs >= vs exact).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Misreading '~> 7.0.2' (allows 7.0.x, not 7.1), or putting a test gem outside its group (loaded in prod).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: A Gemfile lists gems: source, gem 'name', version (~> 7.0 = >=7.0,<8.0), groups (:test). Edit then bundle install.

sections.title: The Dependency List
sections.content: A Gemfile is the file listing the Ruby gems your app depends on. It starts with source https rubygems dot org, where to fetch gems, then gem lines: gem rails, tilde-greater 7.0, a name plus a version constraint. Version constraints: tilde-greater 7.0 means greater-than-or-equal 7.0 and less than 8.0, pessimistic, allowing patch and minor; 7.0.1 pins exact; greater-than-or-equal 7 allows any 7 plus. You group gems with group — gem rspec, group test — so they're not loaded in production, and pin sources for git gems with gem x, github org slash x. After editing, run bundle install to resolve and write Gemfile.lock, which pins the exact versions.

sections.title: Reading a Gemfile
sections.content:
source, gem + version constraint, groups, optional sources.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[source rubygems.org] --> G[gem 'rails', '~> 7.0']
  G --> Gr[group: :test for test-only]
  G --> Gi[github: for git gems]
```

sections.title: A Gemfile
sections.content:
```ruby
source 'https://rubygems.org'         # where to fetch gems

# Version constraints:
gem 'rails', '~> 7.0'    # >= 7.0, < 8.0  (pessimistic; patch+minor)
gem 'pg', '~> 1.4.1'     # >= 1.4.1, < 1.5  (patch only)
gem 'puma', '5.6.4'      # EXACT 5.6.4
gem 'sidekiq', '>= 6'    # any 6+

# Groups (load only where needed):
gem 'rspec-rails', group: :test
group :development, :test do
  gem 'pry-byebug'
  gem 'rubocop', require: false
end

# Git source:
gem 'statesman', github: 'gocardless/statesman'

# Then run: bundle install  (resolves and writes Gemfile.lock)
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Misreading '~> 7.0.2' — it allows 7.0.x, NOT 7.1 (the last part is the bound).
Putting a test gem outside its group — it loads in production (bloat, risk).
Forgetting bundle install after editing the Gemfile (the lock won't update).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: A Gemfile lists the gems your app depends on, starting with source.
gem 'name', version uses constraints: '~> 7.0' (>=7.0, <8.0), exact, or >=.
~> 7.0.2 allows 7.0.x (the last part is the bound), not 7.1 — read it carefully.
Group test/dev gems (:test, :development) so they don't load in production.
After editing, run bundle install to resolve and write Gemfile.lock.
